sections.h2: Where is Raleigh County and how is the land laid out?
sections.html:
Raleigh County is in southern West Virginia, and Beckley is both the county seat and its only city. The county was formed on January 23, 1850, from part of Fayette County and named for Sir Walter Raleigh. It covers 609 square miles, of which 605 are land.

The New River runs along the eastern border. The rest of the county is wooded hills cut by creeks, sloping toward the north and west, with the high point of 3,524 feet near the southern corner.

Beckley sits on a plateau at about 2,400 feet, near the meeting of Interstates 64 and 77 and U.S. 19. Outside the city the county has three towns, Lester, Mabscott and Sophia, plus communities such as Shady Spring, Ghent and Piney View. The seven old magisterial districts were folded into three in the 1970s, so an older deed may name a district like Trap Hill that no longer appears on a map.

sections.h2: How did coal shape Raleigh County and its housing?
sections.html:
Coal built most of what stands in Raleigh County today. Mining of the bituminous seams began in the 1890s, a branch of the Chesapeake and Ohio reached Beckley in 1901, and the Winding Gulf coalfield opened in 1907 almost at Beckley's doorstep.

Once the Virginian Railway started a new line toward Virginia ports in 1908, coal output doubled and then tripled within a few years. The county went from 12,436 people in 1900 to 25,633 in 1910 and 96,273 by 1950.

The 1980s brought mechanization and the loss of thousands of mining jobs. Beckley held up better than smaller communities because it sat at an interstate junction, but the county count has slid since. For a seller, that leaves older houses in places where the original employer is gone.

sections.h2: What does the Raleigh County economy rely on now?
sections.html:
Beckley's economy rests mainly on retail, services and tourism, with health care as the largest visible anchor. The encyclopedia lists four hospitals in the city: Beckley Appalachian Regional Healthcare, Raleigh General Hospital, the Veterans Affairs medical center and Jackie Withrow Hospital.

  • West Virginia University Institute of Technology has used the former Mountain State University campus in Beckley since 2015.
  • Visitor draws include the Exhibition Coal Mine, Grandview Park, Twin Falls State Park and the Winterplace ski resort; part of New River Gorge National Park and Preserve lies in the county.
  • Raleigh County Memorial Airport is served by one airline.

The census estimate for 2025 puts the county at 71,775, down 3.8 percent from 2020.

sections.h2: Who collects and who assesses property tax in Raleigh County?
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Tax Division collects the tax, and the Raleigh County Assessor sets the assessed value. The two offices answer different questions, so call the right one first.

sections.h2: What are the Raleigh County property tax due dates?
sections.html:
Raleigh County follows the statewide calendar: two installments, due September 1 and March 1. Sheriffs issue the tickets on or after July 15 of the tax year.

  • First half is due September 1 and goes delinquent October 1.
  • Second half is due March 1 and goes delinquent April 1.
  • A 2.5 percent discount applies to first-half tax paid before September 1 and second-half tax paid before March 1.
  • Delinquent tax accrues interest at 9 percent per year.

Unpaid real estate tax can end in a lien sale. Under West Virginia Code 11A-3-2, the sheriff prepares a second list by September 10 of parcels still delinquent on September 1, and the liens are certified to the State Auditor on October 31. The owner can redeem before certification by paying taxes, interest and charges, which include $25 for the list and $10 per mailed notice. After certification, redemption goes through the Auditor.

sections.h2: How is a Raleigh County house assessed, and where does the money go?
sections.html:
West Virginia assesses property at 60 percent of market value, and the Raleigh County Assessor's site repeats that the 2026 assessed amounts represent 60 percent of current market value. The tax rate then depends on the class of property.

The State Tax Division publication for tax year 2024 defines Class II as property owned, used and occupied by the owner exclusively for residential purposes, plus owner-occupied farms. Class III is other property outside municipalities and Class IV is other property inside them. It states that the Class II rate is two times Class I, while Classes III and IV are four times Class I. A rental or an empty inherited house does not fit the Class II definition, so ask the assessor how a specific parcel is classed.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Raleigh County assessment?
sections.html:
You challenge it in person during the review window each winter, and the window is short. For 2026 the assessor posted real estate and personal property assessments for inspection from January 30 through February 24, and said corrections must be made in that period.

West Virginia Code 11-3-24 sets the frame: the county commission meets as the board of equalization and review no later than February 1, may adjourn after February 15, and must finish by the last day of February. Anyone who does not ask for relief at that meeting waives the right to a correction for the year, apart from an appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals. A taxpayer who has a hearing can appeal the board's order there, and the burden is a preponderance of the evidence.

The board does not hear questions about classification or taxability. If you think a house is in the wrong class, that goes through a separate protest to the assessor under section 11-3-24a.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption on a Raleigh County home?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners who are 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled. West Virginia Code 11-6B-3 exempts the first $20,000 of assessed value of an owner-occupied homestead, with a two-year state residency test.

The exemption attaches to the home the owner occupied on the July 1 assessment date and applies to the following tax year. If the home passes by deed, will or otherwise, the exemption comes off on the next July 1 unless the new owner qualifies. The Raleigh assessor's site also links a Disabled Veteran Real Property Tax Credit form.

sections.h2: What happens when you sell a Raleigh County house with taxes due?
sections.html:
The sale can still close, but the tax has to be dealt with at or before the deed is recorded.

  • Ask the Sheriff's Tax Office for the status of every ticket on the parcel, including prior years.
  • Have the title company confirm whether the second list or a lien sale is in play.
  • Pay what is owed from proceeds or before closing so the lien does not follow the deed.
  • Record the deed with the county clerk and pay the transfer tax.

Under West Virginia Code 11-22-2, the transfer tax is $1.10 per $500 of value, now kept by the county, plus an additional county tax of 55 cents per $500 unless the county raised it, plus a $20 fee for transfers made for consideration. On a $100,000 deed at those base rates that is $220, $110 and $20, or $350. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed with the tax unpaid.

sections.h2: What do Raleigh County sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers here often hold an older house, an unpaid tax ticket or a property inherited from someone else. With the county down from 96,273 people in 1950 to an estimated 71,775, many heirs end up with property they did not plan on managing.

A cash sale skips repairs and showings, but it does not erase a lien. Whatever route you pick, get the tax status in writing from the sheriff's office first.

faqs.q: When are Raleigh County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Tickets go out on or after July 15, a 2.5 percent discount applies if you pay before each due date, and the halves become delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Raleigh County?
faqs.a: Pay at the Sheriff's Tax Office in the Raleigh County Courthouse in Beckley (304-255-9162), at the Ghent or Glen Daniel offices, or through the online link on the sheriff's tax page. Satellite offices close from 12:00 to 1:00 and can close temporarily.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Raleigh County assessment?
faqs.a: Review your assessment with the assessor during the winter inspection window, which ran January 30 through February 24 in 2026, and raise any correction at the county commission's board of equalization and review, which must finish by the end of February. Missing that meeting waives the correction for the year.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Raleigh County house that has delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax is paid from proceeds or before closing, and the title company should confirm whether the parcel is on the delinquent list that is certified to the Auditor on October 31.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Raleigh County sale?
faqs.a: The grantor, meaning the seller, pays unless the buyer accepts the deed without it being paid. The base rates are $1.10 and 55 cents per $500 of value, plus a $20 fee, unless the county commission has set a higher county rate.
